claims.claim: targetStrategy resolves playback target ob.Target, not node rec/server.Destination
Handler.Dial -> internet.Dial -> transport -> DialSystem. nil sockopt directly uses effectiveSystemDialer; AsIs bypasses LookupForIP
TCP node DNS uses Go net.Dialer.DialContext; UDP node DNS uses Go net.ResolveUDPAddr. No configured Xray dns client for nil/AsIs
TCP uses family partition and dialParallel with default300ms fallback; UDP forResolve prefers an IPv4 answer, otherwise first address. UDP has no address racing/fallback
HY2 chooses a random configured hopping port before first DialSystem; subsequent hops keep resolvedIP. probe firstPort and config basePort do not imply first actual data port

gRPC passthrough target reaches custom DialSystem, authority separate; XHTTP requestURL.Host separate from captured dest; TLS explicit ServerName overrides fallback and Reality explicit ServerName retained

Android Go default prefers cgo getaddrinfo; published JNI has CGO_ENABLED=1 and no netgo tag. Default behavior may be overridden by GODEBUG/controller; current XrayService/LibXrayBridge never call SetDNS

Configured IPv4 DNS servers are routed through proxy by fongmi-xray-dns tag; they are not local bootstrap resolvers for node address. IPv6-only device does not need local IPv4 route/NAT64 just to reach these proxiedDNS servers; proxy egress must be able to reach them. Android/system node resolver must itself work

tests.scope: Actual pinned Xray-core DialSystem; local DNS/IPv6 TCP+UDP peers; nil and AsIs sockopt; TLS ServerName separation; no initialized Xray configuredDNS client
limits: Host Linux, Go customresolver; not Android getaddrinfo/device/NAT64 verification
HY2 QUIC handshake already covered elsewhere; here validates the exact UDP dial branch, not repeats that handshake
Dual-stack UDP prefers returned A even if unreachable; no invented Happy Eyeballs guarantee or Java pre-resolution fix
